note: The shelf list: each chapter's shelf-mates in any library, by Library of Congress and Dewey call number. Rendered as 'Wander the stacks' at a chapter's end (chapter-render.mjs). Ranges are broad on purpose — the point is to stand in the aisle and browse. `tale` is an Aarne–Thompson–Uther tale type where the chapter samples one.

1.subject: Dogs
1.wander: Find the thinnest book on working dogs and read how it describes a nose.

1.subject: Maps
1.wander: Open an old atlas to a place you have never been. Look for what the map leaves blank.

1.subject: Jazz
1.wander: Somewhere on this shelf is a goose who learned it. Pick the book with the most worn spine.

2.subject: Wishes in folklore
2.wander: Walk the folktale shelves and count the books with a wish in them. Stop at three.

2.subject: Sound and echoes
2.wander: Take down a book on acoustics and find the page where a sound comes back late.

2.subject: Trees
2.wander: Find a field guide to trees. Choose one you have walked past without naming.

3.subject: Genies and bottled spirits
3.tale: ATU 331 · The Spirit in the Bottle
3.wander: Look for a tale where the one who was helped is not grateful. There are more than you would think.

3.subject: Paradox
3.wander: Open anywhere and read until something is true twice in opposite directions.

3.subject: Signal processing
3.wander: Find a diagram of a signal before and after sampling. Notice what fell between the samples.

4.subject: Locks and keys
4.wander: Find the drawing of a key's cut. Every notch is an argument about who gets in.

4.subject: Winds
4.wander: Look up the local names for winds. Some places have a wind for every mood of a council.

4.subject: Optics
4.wander: Find a chapter on mirrors and read how an image can be accurate and still reversed.

5.subject: Folk songs
5.wander: Find a songbook and a song about work. Hum the first line under your breath.

5.subject: Bookkeeping
5.wander: Open an old bookkeeping manual to double entry. Two slips, one harvest.

5.subject: Earthquakes and faults
5.wander: Find a map of a fault line. Read about the silence before it moves.

6.subject: Mazes and labyrinths
6.wander: Trace one maze with a finger, never lifting it. Notice where the city would put its lanterns.

6.subject: Glass
6.wander: Find a photograph of old glass holding a light that is not its own.

6.subject: Lighting
6.wander: Look up how lamps were placed along old streets. Count the dark between them.

7.subject: Blueberries
7.wander: Find how berry bushes are pruned. What is cut so that more can grow?

7.subject: Sundials
7.wander: Find a sundial's motto. Many of them are about shadows, and most of them are about debts.

8.subject: Wells
8.wander: Find the drawing of a well in section. Water keeps a face at the top and a depth below.

8.subject: Games of skill
8.wander: Learn one tavern game's rules from the book. Notice which rule is really about trust.

8.subject: Taverns and inns
8.wander: Find an old inn's sign in a picture. Guess what the name promised the thirsty.

9.subject: Puzzles
9.wander: Find a puzzle with one piece missing on purpose. Read how the solver is meant to feel the hole.

9.subject: Mosaics
9.wander: Look closely at a mosaic's shards. Find the one the artist had to break twice.

9.subject: Music theory
9.wander: Find the chapter on rests. A silence is written down, counted, and kept.

10.subject: Bones
10.wander: Find the drawing of the whole skeleton. Name the bone that carries the most and says the least.

10.subject: Structural engineering
10.wander: Find a diagram of load moving through a frame. A hall tells the truth with its weight.

10.subject: Auditing
10.wander: Open to the chapter on evidence. What counts as a finding?

11.subject: The short-sighted wish
11.wander: Find a wish that was granted exactly. Read one page past the granting.

11.subject: Seeds
11.wander: Look up how long seeds can wait. Some wait longer than the people who planted them.

11.subject: Flower gardening
11.wander: Find a flower that blooms before its leaves. Some things arrive before their reasons.

12.subject: Rivers
12.wander: Find where two rivers meet on a map and read both of their names aloud.

12.subject: Place names
12.wander: Look up the name of a river near you. Find the older name underneath it.

13.subject: Shells
13.wander: Find a shell drawn in cross-section. Notice that it is a door that grew.

13.subject: Doors
13.wander: Find a door that has been left open in a photograph. Ask who it is waiting for.

13.subject: Cataloging
13.wander: End where the library describes itself. Read how a new book is given a place, then go give one to something you love.

14.subject: Calendars
14.wander: Find a calendar that once dropped days on purpose. Read what people said they had lost, and whether the fields noticed.

14.subject: Drawing
14.wander: Find a figure drawn in as few lines as will hold it. Count the lines. Notice which one you would miss first.

14.subject: Ants
14.wander: Find a drawing of an ant nest cut open. Trace one street home.

15.subject: Parcel post
15.wander: Find the rules for what may be sent by parcel post. Then find the year someone posted a child.

15.subject: Classification
15.wander: Find where the library shelves a book that is about two things. Ask who decided, and whether the book would agree.

15.subject: Carpentry
15.wander: Find how a door is measured for its frame. Then measure something that is standing still.

16.subject: Housekeeping and kitchens
16.wander: Open an old kitchen manual to the chapter on sculleries. Notice how much space the feast takes and how little goes to the sink.

16.subject: Table etiquette
16.wander: Find a seating chart for a formal dinner. Ask who stood behind the curtain so the places stayed clean.

16.subject: Commons
16.wander: Look up how shared pastures and bakehouses stayed standing. Every plenty hides an uncounted pair of hands.

17.subject: Questionnaires
17.wander: Read a guide to writing survey boxes. Notice what disappears when four corners are forced into yes or no.

17.subject: Archives and filing
17.wander: Find an old cabinet index. Look for the drawer marked Miscellaneous; everything interesting lives there.

17.subject: Probability and coincidence
17.wander: Open to a chapter on rare coincidences. Notice how seldom anyone writes down who owes the next one.

18.subject: Bells and bell towers
18.wander: Find a drawing of a belfry louvre and its clapper. Imagine what happens when the room fills with fine flour.

18.subject: Flour milling
18.wander: Look up how millers keep dust suspended or still. Light in a flour loft behaves like a solid thing.

18.subject: Pantomime
18.wander: Read about a wall built out of nothing but two open palms. Ask whether a rope tied to nothing can still ring.

19.subject: Glazing and window glass
19.wander: Find how linseed putty sets a pane in its sash. Notice how clear glass goes invisible until someone sticks a price on it.

19.subject: Optics and refraction
19.wander: Find a diagram of light passing straight through glass. Ask where the beam snags when the pane carries chalk.

19.subject: Snails
19.wander: Look up how slow grazers clear algae from stone and glass. Patience erases more tariffs than argument.

20.subject: Canal locks
20.wander: Find a cross-section of a canal lock chamber. Two waters never have to become one to let a boat pass.

20.subject: Preserves and jams
20.wander: Look up bitter-orange marmalade and tart berry preserves. Notice what one sharp pinch rescues.

20.subject: Otters
20.wander: Find a natural history of river otters. Read how they ride seams where two currents push against each other.

21.subject: Street paving
21.wander: Look up how cobblestones are laid to shed water. Then imagine reading an entire city fourteen inches off the stones.

21.subject: Olfaction and scent tracking
21.wander: Read how a scent trail breaks around corners and pools near grates. What looks empty at eye level is crowded at the floor.

21.subject: Ants
21.wander: Find a map of foraging trails around obstacles. Small citizens always know where the boots step.

22.subject: Pneumatic tubes and chutes
22.wander: Find a diagram of old brass message tubes beneath a city. Gravity takes the heavy parcel; draft carries the paper back.

22.subject: Copper work
22.wander: Open a tinsmith's handbook to riveted chutes and seams. Notice how copper warms to whatever slides through it.

22.subject: Translation
22.wander: Read an essay on what changes when a message arrives as a description of someone else's bundle.

23.subject: Adult education
23.wander: Look up evening schools for workers after their shift. Notice what grown-ups bring to a bench that children never carry.

23.subject: Pi (Number)
23.wander: Find a book on measuring circles with string and dividers. Read the chapter where the circumference refuses to close on an integer.

23.subject: Choirs and unison singing
23.wander: Open to a page on steady breath and fourths. A held note can quiet a shaky hand better than a ruler.

24.subject: Perspective and framing
24.wander: Find a plate showing four crops of the same scene. Every window tells the truth and contradicts its neighbour.

24.subject: Shutters and joinery
24.wander: Look up hinged masking shutters and theatre flats. Opening two at once always changes the shadow on the floor.

24.subject: Evidence and testimony
24.wander: Read how four honest witnesses can hand in four incompatible scorecards of one quiet walk across a courtyard.

25.subject: Baking and ovens
25.wander: Open a baker's book to brick vaults and yeast fermentation. Feel how a room builds pressure before the door is unlatched.

25.subject: Thermodynamics and vents
25.wander: Find a diagram of radiant hearth heat and flue draft. Everything gathered under one roof asks when to open the vent.

25.subject: Honeybees
25.wander: Read how bees warm a hive together before spring opens. Patience smells of wax and berry steam.

26.subject: Feasts and banquets
26.wander: Look up civic feasts that stretched out into the street. Notice who finally gets a chair when the seating plan gives way.

26.subject: Circles and remainders
26.wander: Open to modular arithmetic and remainders. Sometimes the uneven slice is the only thing that lets a ring turn onward.

26.subject: Prophecy in folklore
26.wander: Find a tale where a prophecy comes true by an ordinary slip at supper, and leaves everyone arguing whether it was luck.
